correctness.rationale: Theorem 2.2 and Corollary 2.17 of the full 2026 source characterize positive β(H) and M_r(H) by pure point spectral bases and forbidden monotone sequences. Continuous f preserves eigenbases of a pure point A, weak scalar monotonicity preserves or reverses the forbidden direction; strict monotonicity gives an inverse on the compact image and hence the converse. For necessity, every reversed pair f(a)>f(b) yields via first/last level crossings decreasing/increasing diagonal sequences with unattained image maximum/minimum, respectively. An increasing scalar pair gives cross-class failures. Any flat interval collapses a diagonal counterexample outside the source class to a scalar operator in both classes. All operators are uniformly bounded between 0 and RI; the sequences have limits not among eigenvalues, so their extrema are truly unattained. No numerical or finite argument is substituted for the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The eight universal scalar-calculus statements are not contained in the inspected full source texts: the 2026 spectral characterization supplies order criteria and one affine complement, and the 2026 density/perturbation article treats additive perturbations. The 2023 article studies the strictly smaller absolute norm-attainment class, and its inaccessible full text creates a named residual priority risk. Explicit one-sided crossings and flat-interval obstructions establish converse directions not supplied by those premises as published statements. No equivalent universal four-arrow-plus-reflection classification was identified in the actual comparison searches. This is not evidence of absolute novelty or independent priority certification.
residual_risks: The full text of Ramesh–Osaka–Udagawa–Yamazaki (2023) was inaccessible despite lawful public and institutional attempts; broad implicit scalar statements within that article cannot be excluded.
Universal scalar-calculus stability may have appeared earlier using eigenvalue well-ordering or hereditary attainment terminology; incomplete indexing is not proof of novelty.

The forward direction follows directly from published order criteria, so the mathematical contribution hinges on the combined necessity and reflection classifications, not on a new spectral characterization.

value.rationale: Norm attainment on every reducing subspace and minimum-modulus attainment are natural spectral rigidity notions with recent complete structure theorems. This result determines, without differentiability, positivity gaps, or injectivity assumptions, the entire class of continuous functional-calculus maps that universally preserve or exchange them, as well as the exact additional rigidity needed to reflect membership. The sharp obstruction is infinite-dimensional and invisible to all finite-spectrum tests: scalar collapse of an infinite diagonal spectral ladder can erase every failure. The eight-way classification is one coherent natural result, not arbitrary pointwise coefficient cases.
